text:
Maya: Heads up — after the 08:45 deploy we're seeing p99 jump from ~120ms to ~540ms on small-seq routes. Canary shows the same pattern.

Igor: saw the alert. any obvious diff in the rollout?

Maya: autotune change landed that tweaks kernel_binding heuristics + microbatch target calculation. diff: 
```diff
- kernel_autoselect: true
- microbatch_target: auto
+ kernel_binding: hint_priority: latency
+ microbatch_target: p95_optimized
```

Sam: oof. that microbatch_target tweak can reduce batching depth and increase KV cache cold misses for short sequences.

Lee: ops-bot shows a bunch of KV cache miss spikes in the same window. p95 stable, tail only.

ops-bot: [alert] route=/v1/generate-smallseq p99=540ms (baseline 120ms), kv_cache_miss_rate=+7.2% vs baseline, deploy=deploy/2026-03-18-08:45

Maya: i'm rolling the change out to 10% canary across two nodes — looks like it propagated further than planned. Initiating rollback now.

Igor: +1 rollback. If we can toggle kernel_autoselect to previous behavior that's fastest. Lee can we flip flag?

Lee: flipping feature flag for autotune -> previous-policy. running: 
```bash
kubectl -n inference set env deploy/runtime-autotuner AUTOTUNE_PROFILE=legacy-heuristic
```

Oncall: triggered rollback: kubectl rollout undo deploy/runtime-autotuner --to-revision=23 (started)

Sam: also disabled the new microbatch_target knob in the configmap so new pods pick up legacy settings.

Maya: monitoring grafana now. tail p99 trending down.

ops-bot: [update] rollback completed on 6/6 pods, canary 0% -> match baseline.

Igor: nice. p99 back to ~130ms now, kv cache miss rate returned to baseline.

Maya: confirmed. Temporary fix done. Need postmortem and stronger perf test for kernel_binding heuristics.

Lee: creating an incident ticket and tagging perf/eval. We'll add an automated canary test: simulate small-seq workload with both kernel hints and microbatch settings and assert p99 < 200ms.

Sam: action items: 1) revert autotune PR until we have KV-aware microbatch simulation, 2) add regression test to CI that runs a quick end-to-end perf harness on a forked runtime, 3) run kernel-selector ablation matrix offline and record p95/p99 per setting.

Igor: also add a rollout guard to prevent wide propagation until we've measured p99 impact on representative canaries. feature-flagged gradual ramp only after perf signoff.

Maya: +1. I'll open the PR revert and link the perf results.

Oncall: leaving a note in the incident timeline with timestamps and commands used.

Sam: quick note — logs showed this pattern: short sequences hit kernel A (fast path) when KV cache warm; kernel binding hint nudged them to kernel B which has better throughput at longer sequences but higher cold-kv overhead. mismatch with microbatch depth caused more cold evictions.

Lee: we should add a telemetry metric: kernel_variant_by_seq_len and kv_cache_effective_hit_ratio; will help catch this earlier.

Maya: agreed. I'll own the postmortem (will include perf graphs, config diff, and suggested canary criteria).

Igor: thanks everyone — great fast rollback. :thumbsup:

Sam: follow-up: schedule a 30m sync with perf + runtime tomorrow to codify the acceptance criteria for kernel heuristics.

Lee: adding to calendar.

Maya: closing the thread here; will post the incident link when the postmortem is up.

Oncall: incident closed (monitoring stable).
